title: Google Pics Brings AI Image Editing Into Workspace
caption: Google Pics brings Gemini-powered image generation and object-level editing to Workspace. The bigger shift is not image generation itself — it is whether AI can make revision cycles faster without taking control away from teams. Swipe for the business implications.

slides.label: CREATIVE TOOLS
slides.headline: Google Pics Brings AI Image Editing Into Workspace

slides.label: WHAT CHANGED
slides.headline: Google is moving image AI from prompt-only generation to targeted editing.
slides.body: Pics lets Workspace users generate imagery, then select a specific object or piece of text and describe only the change they want.

slides.label: THE KEY FEATURE
slides.headline: Change one element. Keep the rest.
slides.body: Instead of regenerating an entire visual after every revision, teams can preserve what works and modify the part that does not.

slides.label: WHY IT MATTERS
slides.headline: The business value is revision speed, not novelty.
slides.body: Marketing work is iterative: copy changes, visual swaps, emphasis shifts and format adaptations. Localized AI edits fit that workflow better than one-shot image generation.

slides.label: THE COMPETITIVE ANGLE
slides.headline: Google’s advantage is distribution inside Workspace.
slides.body: If Pics connects tightly with Docs, Slides and existing collaboration habits, Google can reduce the need to move creative work across multiple tools.

slides.label: WHAT TO WATCH
slides.headline: Three questions decide whether Pics becomes useful at work.
bullets: Are object-level edits dependable enough for brand and product details?
How deeply does Pics connect with Docs, Slides and team workflows?
Can non-designers move quickly without limiting creative professionals?

slides.label: THE BOTTOM LINE
slides.headline: Workplace AI is shifting from open-ended generation to controlled production tasks.
slides.body: Read the full story at businessfuture.today
